Western Digital empowers your passion with storage solutions from portable powerhouses to massive capacity, high performance that RAID systems provide.

For video editing, G-RAID SHUTTLE and G-RAID PROJECT 2 support high-resolution 4K/8K workflows with RAID and Thunderbolt™ 3. Music producers can rely on G-RAID PROJECT 2 or G-DRIVE PROJECT for multi-track sessions and sample libraries. Photographers benefit from G-DRIVE PROJECT and SHUTTLE drives for handling RAW photo libraries with high speed and reliability.

An hour of 4K footage can consume 100–300GB depending on compression and other factors. For large video, photo, or music libraries, drives with 16TB+ are recommended. G-RAID SHUTTLE offer up to 52TB+ of storage for demanding production environments.
Yes. RAID 0 enhances performance, while RAID 1 or 5 adds redundancy to protect your work. G-RAID PROJECT 2 and SHUTTLE drives provide flexible RAID configurations to match your workflow needs.

ArmorATD is a rugged, portable drive ideal for on-the-go backups. G-RAID SHUTTLE is a transportable multi-bay RAID system designed for high-capacity media management, especially in 4K/8K video editing environments.

Yes. G-DRIVE, ArmorATD, and G-RAID PROJECT 2 work with USB-C™–equipped iPads, enabling mobile workflows. For direct recording, drives with Thunderbolt™ 3 or USB-C interfaces support fast data transfers and smooth production. Learn more about Thunderbolt vs USB-C.

Follow the 3-2-1 backup rule: 3 copies of your data, 2 stored locally on different drives, 1 off-site or cloud-based. Drives like G-RAID PROJECT 2 and WD Gold help provide reliable local storage and redundancy.
HDDs like WD Gold or G-RAID SHUTTLE offer higher capacities and are ideal for large media libraries. SSDs provide faster transfer speeds with lower capacity. Learn more about HDD vs SSD for creators.

As used for storage capacity, 1GB = 1 billion bytes and 1TB = one trillion bytes. Actual user capacity may be less depending on operating environment and RAID configuration. For RAID products, storage capacity is based on RAID 0 mode.

Workload Rate is defined as the amount of user data transferred to or from the hard drive. Workload Rate is annualized (TB transferred X (8760 / recorded power-on hours)). Workload Rate will vary depending on your hardware and software components and configurations.
G-DRIVE ArmorATD: Shock resistance up to 1.2m on a carpeted concrete floor for 1TB and 2TB capacities, and up to 1m on a carpeted concrete floor for 4TB, 5TB and 6TB capacities.
IEC 60529 IP54: Based on internal testing. Tested to withstand water splashing against the enclosure; limited dust contact does not interfere with operation. Must be clean and dry before use.
Compatible with iPad devices with USB-C port and iPadOS 14+. Based on internal testing; compatibility may vary based on host device and other factors.

Projected values for model numbers WD261KRYZ, WD242KRYZ, WD221KRYZ and WD203KRYZ. Final MTBF and AFR specifications are based on a sample population and are estimated by statistical measurements and acceleration algorithms under typical operating conditions, workloads of 220TB/year, and 40°C device-reported temperature. Derating of MTBF and AFR will occur above these parameters, up to 550TB/year and 60°C (device reported temperature). MTBF and AFR ratings do not predict an individual drive’s reliability and do not constitute a warranty
